stories.author: yousefh409
stories.title: Launch HN: Vendo (YC S26) – Let users build features on top of your product
stories.groq_label: Users can build and customize features in real-time using plain language, with changes rendered in a sandboxed, brand-native UI without touching the original source code.

Discussion type: – Short:

This product, Vendo (YC S26), aims to let users build features on top of another product. Hacker News commenters generally appreciated the concept of empowering users to extend functionality but questioned its necessity given existing solutions like APIs and MCP access. Commenters highlighted that users can already achieve similar outcomes with tools like Claude and local UIs, raising concerns about the project's uniqueness and added value. Overall, the discussion was mixed, with commenters recognizing potential but questioning whether the project sufficiently differentiates itself from established alternatives.
stories.groq_explain: Vendo lets B2B SaaS companies give their customers a way to build custom features on top of their product without touching the original code. It works by running an AI agent that acts as the user, builds UI components from the product’s own API, and renders them in a sandboxed, brand-friendly space. This solves the problem of customers constantly asking for one-off features, saving dev time and keeping the product clean. It’s quick to set up—just install a package—and scales from simple customizations to full automation across tools, all while keeping control with approvals and audits.

stories.groq_explain: A 125-million-parameter AI model was trained to predict and autocomplete piano music in real time on an iPhone 15, processing about 108 notes per second. The breakthrough came from refining how MIDI data is structured, rigorously cleaning the training data, and using a technique called DPO post-training to improve the model’s responses. The result is an app called RollTab that listens to your MIDI keyboard and instantly suggests musical continuations, like GitHub Copilot but for piano. It matters because it turns a creative tool into something interactive and responsive, making music composition faster and more fluid for players.

This project aims to solve the problem of efficient parallel drafting in language models. Hacker News commenters generally appreciated the technical advancements and performance improvements, particularly the speed and memory efficiency gains. Overall, the discussion was cautiously optimistic, with commenters recognizing both the project's potential and its limitations.
stories.groq_explain: DFlash 2 improves AI model inference by making the drafting process parallel, cutting down the time and cost of generating tokens. It builds on speculative decoding, where a smaller model predicts multiple tokens at once, and the larger model verifies them in a single pass. DFlash 2 makes the drafting itself parallel, boosting throughput by 16–25% with minimal added latency. This matters because AI agents today consume massive amounts of tokens, and faster, cheaper inference is key to scaling them effectively.

stories.groq_explain: OpenRouter, the biggest AI model marketplace, is joining Stripe to combine their tech and scale up faster. The core idea is making AI smarter and more accessible by letting many models compete and thrive, not just one.
